extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, researchers, advocates, and agency staff who read, search, draft, or submit comments on Federal Register documents (users of FederalRegister.gov)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for finding, accessing, drafting, and submitting comments and for preparing Federal Register documents (searching by citation, using Public Inspection, plain-language drafting, accessibility, and proper channels for formal comments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate channels for submitting comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Our 'Site Feedback' tool and Federal Register email addresses are only intended for users to submit technical questions and comments on the functionality of the FederalRegister.gov website. These tools cannot be used to submit comments on rulemaking actions or to petition agencies on public policy issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use site-feedback/email addresses on FederalRegister.gov to submit rulemaking comments. Use Regulations.gov (or the agency-specified docket) for formal comments. FederalRegister.gov’s 'Submit a Formal Comment' feature was implemented to allow commenting without leaving the site by working with Regulations.gov — use that feature or the agency’s official comment submission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Public Inspection page for early access
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Inspection web page on FederalRegister.gov offers a preview of documents scheduled to appear in the next day's Federal Register issue. The Public Inspection page may also include documents scheduled for later issues, at the request of the issuing agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Public Inspection page to access important or complex documents before they publish in the official Federal Register so you can review and prepare timely comments or analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify agency-included links in document text
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency has included links as part of the document text, we activate those links using the text in the document. The link may not work if the link in the published document contained an error or if the target website is no longer at that location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on linked material inside a Federal Register document, verify the target URL and consider that links may be broken or outdated; do not assume links will always resolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the document utility bar (sidebar) to access formats and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The utility bar runs along the left side of the document and scrolls with you down the page. You can access the Public Inspection version and the official electronic format of the published document using the 2 bottom icons. And you can print using the printer icon. Sharing You can share (email, …).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the sidebar icons to switch between Public Inspection and official electronic formats, to print, and to share documents; these tools help access official formats and distribute material for comment or review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search by citation and use advanced search techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: This site has a basic search tool and an advanced search. The basic search box appears in the main navigation at the top every page. The 'Search' pull-down tab in the main navigation shows various search options: Document Search: You can search by citation (for example, enter: '75 FR 12345' or '75 Fed. Reg. 12345').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use correct citation formats and the advanced search options to locate Federal Register documents accurately. Learn and apply the search strategies described in the help documents for complex queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official drafting and IBR handbooks when preparing Federal Register documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Document Drafting & Research: links to Drafting Document Drafting Handbook, Incorporation by Reference (IBR) Handbook, Final Guidance on Implementing the Plain Writing Act of 2010 (PDF), Federal Register Plain Language Tools, PlainLanguage.gov, Thesaurus of Indexing Terms, List of Subjects by CFR Title, GPO Page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Office of the Federal Register’s Drafting Handbook and the IBR Handbook when drafting Federal Register documents; consult these resources to ensure legal/formatting compliance and proper incorporation by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Plain Writing Act guidance and plain-language tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Guidance on Implementing the Plain Writing Act of 2010 (PDF) and Federal Register Plain Language Tools are provided as drafting resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft Federal Register text using plain-language principles as recommended by the Final Guidance and PlainLanguage.gov to improve clarity and public comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify and index documents using the Thesaurus and List of Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Thesaurus of Indexing Terms; List of Subjects by CFR Title are listed under Document Drafting & Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the official thesaurus and lists to select appropriate indexing terms and subjects so documents are discoverable and categorized consistently in the Federal Register and CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite and link to Federal Register documents using prescribed patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Linking to FederalRegister.gov: Federal Register documents can be cited in a variety of ways; various linking patterns are explained with examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When referencing Federal Register content externally, follow the recommended citation and linking patterns to ensure persistent, clear references to the correct document and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save and track documents using MyFR clippings
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov allows users to save documents for later use via a MyFR feature named 'clippings'. Documents can be clipped from either the document’s page or from search results. To clip an item look for the flag icon. A simple click on the flag icon will add the document to your clipboard. A MyFR account is …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a MyFR account and use clippings to collect and manage documents you plan to review or comment on, to help track deadlines and relevant materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic access via REST API and open-source clients
rubrics_metrics.description: REST API & Interactive Documentation: Federal Register data originates with files used to produce print and PDF editions... API Clients: Ruby API Client maintained as a gem; other resources and examples provided. FederalRegister.gov is Open Source; project source code is available on GitHub.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the REST API and official clients for bulk or programmatic access to Federal Register data; review the open-source repositories for implementation details and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure accessibility compliance and provide accessible files
rubrics_metrics.description: We designed this site following Section 508 and W3C accessibility design guidelines. This site uses text-based files and Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF) files, which are text-accessible through the use of Adobe PDF Tools. The OFR and GPO are committed to assisting people with disabilities in …
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare Federal Register materials in accessible, text-based formats (accessible PDFs) and follow Section 508/W3C guidelines; consult the Accessibility page for tools and contact information for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know the legal status: Federal Register publications and FOIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register publications, including the FederalRegister.gov website and the various editions of the daily Federal Register, the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), Federal Register/CFR indexes, and the Public Laws posted on the Federal Digital System (FDsys.gov) are not subject to the request for records provisions of the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that Federal Register and CFR publications are not obtainable via FOIA requests; use the official publication sources for access and archival copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official sources (GovInfo, archives) when FederalRegister.gov is unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: During the funding lapse, FederalRegister.gov is not being supported. If data feeds are not available from GPO, FederalRegister.gov will not be updated, so please use the official edition of the Federal Register on Govinfo (https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/fr). If there is a technical issue with the Public Inspection List, you can view the documents on public inspection at our office in Washington, DC or on archives.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If FederalRegister.gov is not updated or experiences technical issues, consult GovInfo, archives.gov, or the OFR public inspection office to access official documents and public inspection materials.
